utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-06-90-T, the Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Two very brief procedural items before we continue to hear the evidence of the witness in private session. The first, the Office of the Prosecution has inquired as to whether they could confront the witness with statements of upcoming witnesses. The Chamber has considered this question and at the moment sees no problem in such an approach as long as the statements are not sought for admission into evidence because that would change the situation considerably. That's one. Second, before we put what others said to a witness we usually first try to explore what the witness says without knowing what others have said about it. And I also refer to the guidance I gave earlier that for such statements small portions can be read slowly into the transcript. If you keep that in mind, then at this moment there seems to no problem. If, however, you want to have any of these statements admitted or use it in any other way than just to confront the witness, then, of course, you should make an appropriate application. Second, we discussed last week, 23rd of August order to the Lucko Unit. Prosecution was invited to see whether it had a copy in its files.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. There is no copy beyond -- as I said, D739 and P558 were the only documents that come close to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Which apparently are not the documents the witness was testifying about. Now, the witness expressed some concerns, or at least some doubts as to whether he was free to give this document. Of course, the witness, at this moment can't consult with anyone because he is ordered not to do so. Is there any way that the Prosecution could perhaps at short notice seek contact with the Croatian authorities to see whether, either a copy would be -- could be obtained from the Croatian authorities; or whether there would be any objection against the witness to give it to the Chamber. Of course, this should be done as transparently as possible, but may I take it that the Defence teams would have no problems in the Prosecution undertaking this effort? In the lack -- in the absence of any response, there seems to be no objection. Then we turn into private session, and the witness may be brought into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. We will adjourn for the day and we'll resume tomorrow, Tuesday, the 23rd of March, quarter past 2.00, Courtroom I. But I already announce that the first thing we will do tomorrow is return into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When I said "Courtroom I," that was a mistake. We resume in Courtroom III, but we'll turn into private session there as well. We stand adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 23rd day of March, 2010, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.05 p.m.,
